faq_heading: Metrotown condos and townhomes: your questions answered

blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built only from the monthly MLS® figures (SnapStats) for condos and townhomes in Metrotown. No local notes, sold prices, building list or live listing feed yet; see the open items.

Metrotown, Burnaby: 345 condos and townhomes listed at the end of October 2026 and 35 sold in the month, a sales ratio of 10%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. By listings that is number 2 of 35 Burnaby communities for condos and townhomes.

blocks.text: Listings of condos and townhomes in Metrotown fell from 371 in June to 345 in October (−7.0%), and 226 sold across the 5 months. In October the community held 26.4% of Burnaby’s 1,309 condos and townhomes listed.

blocks.text: Metrotown Condos and Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Metrotown is Burnaby's downtown: the City's Burnaby 2050 project page describes Metrotown as the city's downtown and lists it with Brentwood, Lougheed and Edmonds as the four town centres that provide higher-density housing in urban settings.

The condo and townhome market sits on the tower lots around Metrotown Station and Metropolis at Metrotown, and on the residential streets that step down from the station — Kingsway, Central Boulevard, Wilson Avenue, Silver Avenue, Telford Avenue and Nelson Avenue are the addresses the City's current applications name.

blocks.text: Metrotown Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: Tower strata are the stock here: the City's current applications for the Metrotown plan area are high-rise towers — a 72-storey proposal at 4940 Kingsway, a 40-storey proposal at 5978 Wilson Avenue, and two towers of 32 and 28 storeys at 6470 and 6508 Silver Avenue — plus tower-base townhouse forms stated inside some applications.

Townhouse-form stock in Metrotown is mostly two forms: street-fronting townhouses at the base of a tower (the Wilson Avenue application states townhouse-style streetfronting units and the Telford Avenue application states townhouse-style units), and ground-oriented units on the residential streets west of the station.
The older towers' systems, not their names, are the buyer's real check.

blocks.text: Metrotown Condos and Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (Bylaw No. 14815) gives the tower stock its districts: Low-Rise Apartment (R3, R4), Mid-Rise Apartment (R5, R6) and High-Rise Apartment 1 and 2 (R7, R8), with Townhouse District (R2) separate for ground-oriented forms.

blocks.text: Metrotown Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The R2 extension made Metrotown Station a two-region terminus on September 7, 2026: TransLink states the extended R2 runs from Park Royal to Metrotown Station all day, seven days a week, and replaced the peak-only 222 Willingdon Express, so the station now serves a North Shore commute, not only an Expo Line commute.

A new pedestrian rule is being built at the station: the City states construction began in May 2026 on Burnaby's first pedestrian scramble crossing, at Central Boulevard and the Metrotown underground parkade access, one of the city's busiest pedestrian areas.

blocks.text: Metrotown Condos and Townhomes: development and new projects

items.t: Concord Metrotown — Sky Park, 4866 Kingsway and 4833 Metro Way (Concord Pacific): Central Tower and West Tower, strata lots 1 to 722, per the developer's own disclosure statement; Sixth Amendment dated August 14, 2026. Status: disclosure amendment filed (as of November 3, 2026).

4940 Kingsway proposal (REZ #24-16, applicant DIALOG): approximately 72-storey high-rise at portion of 4940 Kingsway and 6446 and 6450 Nelson Avenue, 169 market strata homes, 130 non-market rental homes, 170 market rental homes.

5978 Wilson Avenue (REZ #24-22, Bosa Properties Inc.): 40-storey mixed-use building with residential, commercial and childcare. Status: Third Reading and Final Adoption October 27, 2026 (as of November 3, 2026).

6470 and 6508 Silver Avenue (REZ #25-12): two residential towers of 32 and 28 storeys, about 784 units including 83 rental-replacement units. Status: First and Second Reading June 23, 2026 (as of November 3, 2026).
Metropolis at Metrotown conceptual master plan (REZ #18-27, Ivanhoe Cambridge): 1700 and 4800 Kingsway and portion of 4750 Kingsway.

blocks.text: Metrotown Condos and Townhomes: costs and taxes

items.t: The City's 2026 Class 1 Residential rate for a Metrotown condo is 1.72223 per $1,000 of taxable value (components: General Government 0.34287, Community Safety 0.71869, Engineering 0.20592, Parks, Recreation, Culture and Library 0.39555, Growth Infrastructure Investment 0.05920), per the Burnaby Rates Bylaw 2026 (Bylaw No. 14814), adopted May 12, 2026.

blocks.text: Metrotown Condos and Townhomes: getting around

items.t: Metrotown Station (Expo Line) is the rapid-transit anchor; its bus exchange is where the local routes for the south-side streets begin, including the 116 to Edmonds Station.
The R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus now terminates at Metrotown Station and runs 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. seven days a week, every 6 to 7 minutes at weekday peak and every 10 to 15 minutes off-peak.
The 116 runs between Metrotown Station and Edmonds Station, so the south-side streets have a direct bus to Edmonds without the SkyTrain.

blocks.text: Metrotown Condos and Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: For an older tower, the depreciation report is the systems check: the Province tracks updated depreciation report requirements effective July 1, 2024, and the October 27, 2025 expansion of who may prepare them, so a report dated before that change was prepared under the older rules.

A buyer of a tower-base townhouse should confirm the strata plan: the unit is a strata lot in the tower strata, with the tower's parkade, elevators and envelope in its depreciation report, even though the unit's entrance is at street level.

blocks.text: Metrotown home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

410 condos sold in Metrotown with a median price of $690,000 (the middle half sold between $580,000 and $815,750), taking a median of 31 days to sell at 97.0% of the last list price; 8% sold above list. They had a median $909 per square foot, a median year built of 2017 and a median strata fee of $426 a month. 31 townhomes sold in Metrotown with a median price of $979,000 (the middle half sold between $734,000 and $1,142,500), taking a median of 39 days to sell at 97.2% of the last list price; 3% sold above list. They had a median $800 per square foot, a median year built of 2016 and a median strata fee of $369 a month.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Metrotown?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 345 condos and townhomes listed in Metrotown. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Metrotown a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In October 2026, condos and townhomes in Metrotown had a sales ratio of 10%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Metrotown from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 226 condos and townhomes sold in Metrotown over those 5 months, out of 916 in all of Burnaby.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did condos in Metrotown sell for?
faq.a: 410 condos sold in Metrotown between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $690,000.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Metrotown?
faq.a: The median was 31 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.0% of the last list price (8% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
